messages:
anya: FYI we hit a token-id shift after merging Solstice LoRA + int4 quant. Invoice extraction examples show placeholders instead of vendor names. Suspect finetune used a different SentencePiece build.

bryce: Can you share a tiny repro so we can confirm tokenizer mismatch vs quant artifact?

anya: Repro command I used: `python eval_pack/run_eval.py --pack solstice_invoice_200 --model merged_solstice_lora --quant int4`

anya: Small example pasted:
INPUT: "Invoice total: $123.45
Vendor: Acme Consulting"
FP16: "Vendor: Acme Consulting"
INT4 (post-merge): "Vendor: <unk> Consulting"
Token diff: token("Vendor") id 102 fp16 vs id 105 int4-run.

li: Pattern looks like a deterministic id offset for a contiguous token range. Did the finetune use spm_v1 vs base spm_v2?

anya: Yes, finetune metadata shows tokenizer_version: spm_v1. The base model uses spm_v2.

nate: We have two remediation flows: (1) remap LoRA embeddings to base vocab ids at merge time (fast), or (2) retokenize finetune data and retrain LoRA (more intrusive but clean).

anya: I tried the remap path with our utility: `tools/tokenmap/rebase_lora.py --lora lora_solstice.pt --remap spm_v1_to_v2.json --out lora_solstice_remapped.pt`  it completes. Can @eval-bot run a quick pack comparing fp16, int4_raw, int4_remapped on staging?

eval-bot: queued run 5109876560: solstice_invoice_200 on merged_solstice fp16, int4_raw, int4_remapped. ETA ~14m. Results will land under /runs/5109876560.

nate: Interim numbers from staging UI: fp16 EM=0.93, int4_raw EM=0.59, int4_remapped EM=0.87. Token-overlap heatmap shows a consistent +3 id offset for tokens with ids between 90-160 prior to remap. Remap recovers most cases.

bryce: Good. For remaining failures we should try a surface-string fallback: when an id maps to OOV during remap, run spm.encode(surface) and insert best-effort mapping. Also consider a tiny calibration pass that nudges LoRA deltas for newly mapped ids.

li: I'll prototype a fallback: map_by_surface.py that falls back to base spm.encode and logs ambiguous mappings. Also adding a 50-prompt adversarial subset of customer templates (dates, invoice codes, vendor variants) to catch edge cases.

anya: Proposal: 1) add remap step to merge pipeline with a --remap json if tokenizer mismatch detected, 2) include surface-fallback and small calibration option, 3) add quick-regression check to solstice_invoice_200 that asserts EM_loss(fp16 -> int4_remapped) <= 0.05. I'll open a PR with repro commands and the 50-adversarial vectors.

bryce: :thumbsup: Also update onboarding checklist for SEs: "confirm tokenizer_version parity or supply remap.json". That will cut down silent failures.

anya: Will attach sample logs and exact repro in the PR. If folks want to run extra comparisons (retokenize versus remap+calibration), I can spin them up on staging.

nate: One more note: add a warning in the console when merging a LoRA whose tokenizer metadata != base. Block by default unless user opts-in to automatic remap.

li: Agree. I'll draft the gating logic and add unit tests for remap tool.

anya: Thanks team.
